column1: # 60 fps: Unreal's own limit, found by name in main by the rewriter (ue_cvar.py; main.fixups.tsv UE_CVAR:t.MaxFPS 0x7584630, which is
# FPSLocker's t.MaxFPS object for this build 0x7584640 minus its +0x10 value pointer). hle_fpslock.c writes the game thread's and the
# render thread's copies every frame they differ, and rhi.SyncInterval (0x7455a40) 2 -> 1 vsync. The present cap at 60 makes the host
# present one vsync a frame (hle_nvn.c present_itv), so neither the game's present interval 2 nor a display-mode cut is needed.
# 120 is a runtime rung (settings.tsv's `120=120 fps?DM_GAME_FPS_MAX==120&platform:mac`): fps_max only unlocks it, the default stays 60.
# fps_high() (hle_nvn.c) refuses 120 without an engine limiter the host writes; this title HAS one (UE_CVAR:t.MaxFPS in main.fixups.tsv,
# dm_fps_lock_engine true) and has no frame step page (dm_fps_state 0), so the gate passes with this key at 120.
# the engine's limiter sleeps a whole frame period (1/MaxFPS) and subtracts none of the frame's work, so any value near the target lands after the
# host's 60 Hz tick and costs a tick: measured in one run on this build (p50 frame time) t.MaxFPS 60 -> 33.45 ms (30.0 fps), 61 -> 21.0, 120 -> 22.6-25.4,
# 240 -> 17.0, 0 -> 16.48 (60.7 fps). So the host writes 0 (no engine limit) and its present cap at 60 paces the frames; the game steps by the time that
# passed, so 60 is the same speed as 30 (FPSLocker's 60 fps patch for this build does the same: its ALL_FPS entry writes t.MaxFPS and r.VSync only).
# the game calls nvnDeviceSetDepthMode with near = 0 in the check boot: the pipeline bases made before it runs are made for that mode
